title: Equivalent Expressions by Graphing: Graph Match
description: Identify equivalent single-variable expressions by renaming the variable x when needed, graphing the original, and comparing each answer-choice graph, including expressions written in function notation.

blocks.html:
Give it a try

Spend about a minute on this question. Keep what you tried, even if you got stuck. You can continue without submitting an answer.

  1. \(\frac{2x^2-x+10}{x^2+3x-4}\)
  2. \(\frac{2x^2+x-10}{x^2+3x-4}\)
  3. \(\frac{2x^2-x-10}{x^2+3x-4}\)
  4. \(\frac{2x^2+x+10}{x^2+3x-4}\)

content.html:
Compare paths instead of combining fractions

The opening expression has three fractions, two products to expand, and a subtraction to track. Graph Match lets you compare the original with each choice as written.

We’ll start with two short expressions so you can see what a matching path looks like, then return to these fractions.

content.hint: Keep the first row visible. Hide and show the second row while watching several places along the line.
content.prompt: Show both \(2(x+1)\) and \(2x+2\). What happens when you toggle the second line?
choices: It crosses the first line and then follows a different path.
It covers the first line, leaving the same path on screen.
It runs parallel to the first line along a different path.
It meets the first line at zero and then curves away.
content.solution:
Show \(2(x+1)\), then show \(2x+2\) as well.
Hide and show the second line. Its color may cover the first, but the path does not change.
The second line covers the first line: choice B.
content.explanation: The color may change, but the path stays put. Both rows give the same height at each input, so the two lines lie on top of each other.

content.html:
A match keeps the same path

Equivalent expressions have the same output at every allowed input, so their graphs overlap.

Click the colored circle at the left of an expression to show or hide its graph. Toggling helps you see whether one path covers another.

Check beyond the shared points

Show \(x^2-4\) and \(2(x^2-4)\). Both meet the x-axis at -2 and 2. Compare their heights between those points. Do the paths stay together?

content.hint: Look at the two heights on the vertical axis. Does the same input produce the same output there?
content.prompt: The graphs of \(x^2-4\) and \(2(x^2-4)\) share both x-intercepts but separate between them. What does this show?
choices: The expressions match because their two x-intercepts agree.
The expressions match because both curves have the same shape.
The expressions match because both graphs contain a squared term.
The expressions differ because their heights disagree at some inputs.
content.solution:
At \(x=0\), the original graph has height \(-4\), while the comparison graph has height \(-8\).
One disagreement is enough to rule out equivalence, even though the two zeros match.
Choose D: the expressions differ.
content.explanation: Matching zeros do not make matching expressions. The height difference at \(x=0\) rules this choice out; Graph Match requires the whole path to agree.

content.html:
Use x, Graph, Compare

  1. Replace the single input letter with x throughout, if needed.
  2. Graph the original expression on its own row.
  3. Graph each choice on another row and compare its path with the original.

Keep the original visible. Hide a candidate before trying the next. Inspect several parts of the allowed region; one shared point is not enough.

Try the comparison controls

The original is \((x+1)(x-3)\). Enter \(x^2-2x-3\) on another row. Toggle it off and on to see the same path beneath it.

Then try \(x^2+2x-3\). It shares one point with the original but separates elsewhere.

calculator.title: Type and compare A through D

content.hint: Several choices pass through the same point on the vertical axis. Compare their paths to the left and right as well.
content.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to \(2x(x-3)+4(x-3)\)? Keep the original visible and graph each choice on a separate row.
content.solution:
Keep \(2x(x-3)+4(x-3)\) visible.
Enter each choice on a new row, hiding the previous candidate as you go.
The graph of \(2x^2-2x-12\) follows the original; toggling it leaves the same curve underneath.
B and C separate from the original away from the vertical axis. D is shifted upward.
Choose A.
content.explanation: A traces the original curve. The SAT's sign and missing-term traps in B and C keep the same height at \(x=0\), so that one point cannot pick the answer; D has the wrong constant and sits higher.

content.html:
Keep fractions grouped

For \((3x+5)/(x-2)\), put the complete numerator and denominator in parentheses. If the question says x>2, compare the graphs to the right of 2.

content.hint: Compare just to the right of 2 as well as farther along the curve. Keep the entire denominator grouped.
content.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{3x+5}{x-2}\) for \(x>2\)? Graph the candidates and compare to the right of \(2\).
content.solution:
Keep \(\frac{3x+5}{x-2}\) visible.
Enter each candidate on another row and compare to the right of 2.
The curve for \(3+\frac{11}{x-2}\) covers the original throughout that region. The others separate.
Select B. No long division is needed to find the match.

calculator.title: Compare near and away from x = 2

content.explanation: B gives the matching curve. A fails to account for the denominator's shift, C has the wrong remainder, and D puts the subtraction outside the fraction. Far to the right, some curves get close; checking near \(x=2\) exposes the differences.

content.html:
Change only the input letter

For \((2p+1)/(p-3)\), type \((2x+1)/(x-3)\). Replace p with x in every candidate too, keeping all signs, numbers, and parentheses.

Use lowercase x for Graph Match. A leftover p can become a slider instead.

content.title: Build the fraction graph yourself

feedback.solution_html: Enter (2x+1)/(x-3) on one row. It should display as \(\frac{2x+1}{x-3}\). Keep it visible and check again.

targeted_hints.message_html: Replace every p with lowercase x. Do not add a p or capital X slider.
This check needs one visible expression: the original fraction. Hide or remove extra rows.
Enter the fraction and leave its graph visible.

feedback.retry_message_html: Check both copies of the input letter and both pairs of parentheses. The denominator is the whole expression x minus 3.

attempt_based_hints.message_html: Type the whole numerator in parentheses, then /, then the whole denominator in parentheses.

feedback.success_message_html: Nice work! The fraction is ready to compare: the input letter changed, and both groups stayed intact.

content.instructions_html: Replace p with lowercase x in \((2p+1)/(p-3)\). Graph the expression, grouping the numerator and denominator.

content.html:
Keep the whole root together

For \(\sqrt{18t^2}\), type sqrt(18x^2). Compare it with \(3x\sqrt2\). They overlap for positive inputs but separate for negative ones.

If the question says t>0, compare only that region. Group fractional exponents too: type x^(3/2).

content.hint: Keep the square inside the original root. Compare at several positive inputs; the curves may agree at one convenient value.
content.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to \(\sqrt{8r^2}\) for \(r>0\)? Use \(x\) for \(r\) and compare the positive-input graphs.
content.solution:
Graph \(\sqrt{8x^2}\).
Graph each candidate using x instead of r, and compare to the right of 0.
The line for \(2x\sqrt{2}\) covers the original there. A is too steep, B curves away, and D is below the horizontal axis.
Select C, \(2r\sqrt{2}\).
content.explanation: C matches on the required positive inputs. A mishandles the factor under the root, B loses the squared input, and D has the wrong sign for a square root. At \(x=1\), B happens to agree, so one point would be a trap.

content.html:
Build the original from function definitions

Define \(f(x)=x+2\), \(g(x)=2x-1\), and \(h(x)=3x+4\). Then type f(x)*g(x)-h(x) to graph the requested combination.

Hide the individual function graphs, keeping their definitions. Compare choices with the combination’s graph.

content.hint: The original row should multiply f and g before subtracting h. Comparing a choice with f or g alone answers a different question.
content.prompt: Let \(f(x)=x+2\), \(g(x)=2x-1\), and \(h(x)=3x+4\). Which expression is equivalent to \(f(x)\cdot g(x)-h(x)\)? Enter the combination, then compare its graph with the choices.
content.solution:
The three definition rows are already present. Leave them hidden.
Enter \(f(x)\cdot g(x)-h(x)\) as the original graph.
Enter each choice separately. The curve for \(2x^2-6\) covers that combination.
Select D.

calculator.title: Graph the combination before the choices

content.explanation: D matches the requested combination. A adds h instead of subtracting it; B groups the original as f times (g minus h); C adds f and g instead of multiplying. Desmos can perform the combination as written, so you do not have to expand it by hand.

content.html:
Use the operation the question names

After defining \(f,g\), type f(x)/g(x) for a quotient. Keep the definitions and compare candidates with that one quotient graph. For x>2, inspect the part to the right of 2.

content.hint: Graph the entire quotient before testing the choices, then compare to the right of 2. A shared denominator alone does not make two outputs equal.
content.prompt: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by \(f(x)=x^3-4x\) and \(g(x)=x^2-x-2\). Which expression is equivalent to \(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\) for \(x>2\)?
content.solution:
Use the two hidden definitions, then enter \(f(x)/g(x)\).
Graph each candidate and compare to the right of 2, toggling candidates one at a time.
The graph of \(\frac{x(x+2)}{x+1}\) matches the quotient. The other three separate from it.
Select A.
content.explanation: A gives the matching quotient graph on x > 2. B drops an x factor, C changes a sign, and D drops the remaining numerator factors.

content.html:
Put one function inside another

Composition, written \(f(g(x))\), means use g first and feed its result into f.

Define \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+4}\) and \(g(x)=2x+1\), then graph f(g(x)). Compare it with \(\sqrt{2x+5}\). Keep the order: g(f(x)) describes a different operation.

content.hint: The function acting on the original input sits inside the parentheses of the function that acts second.
content.prompt: The question asks for the result of applying \(g\) first and then applying \(f\) to that output. After defining both functions, which row graphs the requested rule?
content.solution:
Start with the input x.
Applying g first gives g(x).
Applying f to that result places the whole g(x) inside f: f(g(x)).
Enter that row: choice D.
content.explanation: The inside function acts first. A reverses the order; B multiplies two outputs; C adds them. Those are three different rules, even though all use the same two definitions.

content.hint: Use f(g(x)) as the original row. Keep the square root’s full input together, and compare on x ≥ 0.
content.prompt: Let \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+6}\) and \(g(x)=3x-2\). For \(x\ge0\), which expression is equivalent to \(f(g(x))\)? Graph the composition before comparing choices.
content.solution:
Keep \(f(x)=\sqrt{x+6}\) and \(g(x)=3x-2\) as hidden definitions.
Enter \(f(g(x))\) as the original graph.
Enter each choice and compare from x = 0 to the right. \(\sqrt{3x+4}\) covers the original curve.
Select B.
content.explanation: B matches the composition. A reverses the function order, C moves the added 6 outside the root, and D multiplies outputs.

blocks.html:
Return to the three fractions

Try the opening question again. Use the graphs to find the matching expression.

content.prompt: Which expression matches the original for the allowed inputs?
content.hint: Graph the complete original as one expression. Keep each full numerator and denominator grouped, and compare the candidates to the right of x=1.
content.solution:
Graph \((x+2)/(x-1)+(2x-3)/(x+4)-(x^2+1)/((x-1)(x+4))\).
Add each choice on another row; hide it before testing the next. Compare several parts of the region \(x>1\), including near \(x=2\) and \(x=4\).
Only D, \((2x^2+x+10)/(x^2+3x-4)\), covers the original path throughout that region.
content.explanation: D matches. The paths overlap in the allowed region, so you identified the equivalent expression without combining the three fractions.

content.prompt: A question uses \(f(t)\) and \(g(t)\), asks for \(f(g(t))\), and says \(t>1\). Recall Graph Match: how do you compare the choices?
choices: Use x throughout; define f and g; graph f(g(x)); compare each choice to the right of 1 and select the matching curve.
Use x throughout; define f and g; graph g(f(x)); compare each choice to the right of 1 and select the matching curve.
Use x throughout; define f and g; graph f(x) times g(x); compare each choice to the right of 1 and select a matching curve.
Use x throughout; define f and g; graph f(g(x)); compare each choice at x = 2 and select the first matching point.
content.explanation: Use x consistently, graph the exact requested rule, and compare curves in the region the question specifies. B reverses the composition, C replaces it with multiplication, and D stops at one shared point.

blocks.html:
Try it on your own

Choose the approach for each question. Try these now or save them for homework.

content.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to \(\sqrt{27r^3}\) for all \(r>0\)?
content.explanation: Graph \(\sqrt{27x^3}\), then each choice using x instead of r. Compare to the right of 0. C, \(3x\sqrt{3x}\), follows the original curve. A loses a factor of the input under the root, B is scaled too high, and D grows too quickly. A and D happen to match at x = 1, so compare farther along the curve. Select C.

content.prompt: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by \(f(x)=\frac{2}{3}x+1\) and \(g(x)=3x-4\). Which expression is equivalent to \(f(x)\cdot g(x)\)?
content.explanation: Define f and g as given, hide their individual curves, and graph f(x)*g(x). B, \(2x^2+\frac{1}{3}x-4\), covers the product. A reverses the middle term's sign, C loses a negative sign during multiplication, and D drops the middle term. All four choices pass through the same point at x = 0, so comparing that point alone cannot decide the answer.

content.prompt: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by \(f(t)=\frac{1}{t-2}\) and \(g(t)=3t+1\). For \(t>1\), which expression is equivalent to \(f(g(t))\)?
content.explanation: Use x throughout: define \(f(x)=1/(x-2)\) and \(g(x)=3x+1\). Graph \(f(g(x))\), then each candidate, and compare to the right of 1. A, \(1/(3x-1)\), covers the composition there. B uses 1/g(x-2), C graphs g(f(x)), and D multiplies outputs. Select A in the original letter t.

content.html:
Graph Match

Compare the whole path within the region the question allows.
